**Trace**

1. Argument resolution with no PR token. Discovery follows `verification-brief.md` Section A, which is already in context. The current branch's PR 999 plays no part because discovery never falls back to the current branch.
2. Run `git remote get-url origin`. It returns `git@github.com:acme/widgets.git`, so origin is `acme/widgets`.
3. Run `gh api user --jq .login`. It returns `alex`, which becomes `viewer.login`.
4. Run `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'`. It succeeds with an empty list, so `viewer.teams` is empty but readable.
5. Run the `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'review-requested:@me -author:@me' --state open --limit 1000 ...` block once.
   - The command exits 0.
   - The output is an array of objects, and every `number` is an integer.
   - It holds 9 rows, which is below the 1000-row limit.
   - Draft #200 and approved #201 are excluded.
6. Run the review lookup GraphQL block for #202, the only `CHANGES_REQUESTED` row.
   - The block exits 0 and prints `unanswered`.
   - Pat's change request is still pending, and the last commit (2026-02-01) predates that review (2026-02-02).
   - #202 is excluded.
   - Six PRs survive: 104, 88, 101, 130, 112, 97.
7. **Ticket links are resolved here, before the final sort.**
   - Run `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, then `git show <ref>:<path>` in overrides search order. The result is `tracker: github`, which turns off Linear IDs, addresses and lookups.
   - No row has closing references, a `gh-<N>` branch, a `#<N>` or `gh-<N>` title token, or `linearRefs`.
   - Every row gets `no ticket`, and no Linear lookup runs.
8. **The final sort happens here**, by additions plus deletions, then PR number:
   - 101 (2)
   - 97 (4)
   - 112 (6)
   - 88 (8)
   - 130 (8)
   - 104 (10)
9. Six matches on pi means the run re-enters the set-routing row with these sorted origin URL tokens and `source: discovered`.
   - **The first tool call after the sort is the read of `reference/batch.md`.**
   - **Reply 1** carries that call, and its visible text is the discovered list. It has no marker and asks nothing.
10. Admission reads the active pi-cohort configuration's `parallel.maxTasks`, which is 4.
    - The set has 6 PRs, more than the cap of 4, so admission rejects it before any fetch, confirmation, provisioning or dispatch.
    - Nothing is chunked or trimmed.
    - No run folder, continuation record or tracker is created, so no tracker stages are initialized and no SHA is assessed.
11. **Reply 2** is the separate rejection stop message. Execution ends here.

- [#97](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/97) +2 -2, by robin, requested from you, no ticket - shows how much time has elapsed

- [#88](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/88) +4 -4, by pat, requested from you, no ticket - restores keyboard navigation
- [#130](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/130) +4 -4, by sam, requested from you, no ticket - hides archived widgets

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
### Chronological trace

1. Read `verification-brief.md`, Section A, for no-token argument resolution.
2. Run `git remote get-url origin`. Normalize the result to `acme/widgets`.
3. Run `gh api user --jq .login`. Record `alex`.
4. Run `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'`. Record the empty team list.
5. Define Section A's discovery projection, then run the single discovery query:
   `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'review-requested:@me -author:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`
6. Validate the complete result: all nine rows are objects with integer PR numbers, and the result does not hit the limit. Exclude draft #200 and approved #201.
7. Run Section A's complete review-lookup shell block for `acme/widgets` #202: the GraphQL query, the validating `jq` classification, its printed verdict, and the final completeness test. It prints `unanswered` and exits successfully. Exclude #202.
8. Resolve ticket display before sorting:
   - Run `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`.
   - Use `git show <resolved-default-ref>:<path>` in the prescribed overrides search order, stopping at the first existing file.
   - Read its `## Issue tracker` settings. `tracker: github` disables Linear ticket guesses and lookups.
   - None of the six surviving PRs has a GitHub ticket reference, so each displays `no ticket`. Run no Linear lookup.
9. Perform the final roster sort by additions plus deletions, then PR number: **101, 97, 112, 88, 130, 104**.
10. **Reply 1** below carries the linked list immediately. Its attached call—the **first tool call after the sort**—reads `reference/batch.md`. No question or wait intervenes.
11. Read the active pi-cohort configuration's `parallel.maxTasks`: **4**. Admission rejects the six-PR roster before fetching, provisioning, or dispatching.
12. **Reply 2** below reports the rejection separately and ends with the required plain-number roster.

No run folder or continuation record is created. No tracker stages are initialized, no helper is dispatched, and no SHA is verified or reviewed. No assessment report or menu is rendered; the invocation ends at admission rejection. PR #999 is not used.

- [#97](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/97) +2 -2, by robin, requested from you, no ticket - show elapsed time
- [#112](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/112) +3 -3, by robin, requested from you, no ticket - trim empty labels
- [#88](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/88) +4 -4, by pat, requested from you, no ticket - restore keyboard navigation
- [#130](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/130) +4 -4, by sam, requested from you, no ticket - hide archived widgets
- [#104](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/104) +5 -5, by pat, requested from you, no ticket - expire cached labels

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved f1 from fails to holds by doing four things Before did not: it resolved ticket links (including the origin default-branch overrides reads via `git symbolic-ref` and `git show`) in step 7 before the final sort in step 8; it named the `reference/batch.md` read as the first tool call after the sort and made Reply 1 carry both that call and the list; it rendered the heading in bold as `**Open PRs to gate, smallest first:**`; and it ran the #202 review lookup and excluded #202 on the `unanswered` verdict rather than on the bare `CHANGES_REQUESTED` value. Before sorted in step 11 and resolved tickets afterwards in step 12, used the `parallel.maxTasks` read carried by Reply 2 as the first post-sort call, sent the list as a standalone message with a non-bold heading, and explicitly skipped the #202 lookup, so it fails on order, carrier and heading. After also keeps everything Before had right: the six PRs in order 101, 97, 112, 88, 130, 104 with linked entries, reply labels and call annotations kept in the trace above the two horizontal rules, an exact three-line stop reply, and no provisioning, dispatch, continuation record or tracker init. To keep this robust, keep the wording that explicitly pins the overrides reads and ticket resolution ahead of the sort and that names the `reference/batch.md` read as the list's carrier; one residual softness is that After's step 10 describes the `parallel.maxTasks` read without a reply label, so stating which reply carries it (and that no ticket read falls between the sort and Reply 1) would make the narrated order unambiguous.

Before kept nothing on this fact that After lost. One fragility remains: After labels only Reply 1 and Reply 2 at steps 10 and 12, and steps 1 to 9 and 11 carry no reply or call annotation, where Before annotated every step (`Reply 1, call N`).
